handoff.purpose: Defines fingerprinting functions for task identity and the attempt_history function to query ledger for past attempts.

symbols.name: _definition_fingerprint
symbols.note: Internal function to compute a SHA256 fingerprint of a task definition including instruction, base_revision, target_paths, and gate.

symbols.name: _candidate_definition_fingerprint
symbols.note: Computes definition fingerprint from a Candidate object, extracting gate fields.

symbols.name: attempt_history
symbols.note: Public function that queries the ledger for attempt history by task_ids; opens ledger read-only and returns (history, error).

claims.text: A queue task is not the same work merely because its prose stayed the same: a new candidate base, target scope, or executable gate changes the proposition being attempted.
claims.why: The function includes base_revision, target_paths, and gate in the fingerprint when present, and falls back to instruction-only fingerprint only when all are absent.

claims.text: Legacy tasks declare none of these fields and retain the historical instruction-only fingerprint exactly.
claims.why: When base_revision, target_paths, and gate are all empty/falsy, the function returns instruction_fingerprint(instruction) directly.
The code passes read_only=True to SpineLedger constructor.

claims.text: The normal constructor creates the parent directory, sets journal_mode=WAL (a file write) and runs migrations inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so opening a ledger to look at it MUTATES it -- unacceptable in --dry-run, whose entire contract is that it changes nothing.
claims.why: This claim refers to the behavior of SpineLedger constructor without read_only, which is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: SQLite enforces that here; this function does not merely promise it.
claims.why: The enforcement mechanism is not visible; it depends on SpineLedger's implementation with read_only=True.

claims.text: Returns (history, error) and NEVER raises: a missing ledger (a fresh checkout has attempted nothing) is an empty history, not a failure.
claims.why: If db_path does not exist, returns ({}, None). The function catches Exception and returns error string. No unhandled exceptions in visible code.

claims.text: The error string is surfaced as a queue note, because silently degrading to 'no memory' is exactly how a loop would go back to repeating itself without saying so.
claims.why: The usage of the error string as a queue note is outside this chunk.

claims.text: A LIKE match is a substring test; confirm the row really is one of the ids asked for rather than one that merely contains it.
claims.why: After retrieving intents, the code explicitly checks 'if task_id not in wanted: continue' to filter out substring matches.

observations.what: Function _definition_fingerprint references instruction_fingerprint which is not defined in this chunk.
attempt_history uses ATTEMPT_INTENT_KIND without definition or import in this chunk.
attempt_history accesses intent.resolved_ts, intent.created_ts, intent.state, intent.result, intent.payload which are not defined in this chunk.
attempt_history imports SpineLedger and default_db_path inside the function; this is fine but unusual.
